research_question: Can intrinsic protection of B's independent veto be distinguished from A's private self-image payoff when A would gain from overriding B and there is no audience, accountability, exit leverage or future instrumental utility?
source_selection: 8 purposively selected relevant original publications/working paper. NOT an exhaustive search, original-author full-text audit of all papers or first discovery in repository.

sources.title: The Intrinsic Value of Decision Rights
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: Self decision rights often carry noninstrumental value.
sources.nonimplication: Own control preferences do not identify costly respect for an independent other agent's continued choice.

sources.title: Do people intervene to make others behave prosocially?
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: Among those who would donate, only a minority ban the other chooser's selfish option; allowing initial choice affects acceptability.
sources.nonimplication: Refraining from intervention is not proof of costly protection when unilateral exploitation is profitable and sanctionless.

sources.title: What Motivates Paternalism? An Experimental Study
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: Choice architects frequently remove options and may project their own aspirations into others' choices.
sources.nonimplication: Belief that intervention helps B is not proof of B's informed authorization or own independent goal preservation.

sources.title: Exploiting moral wiggle room: experiments demonstrating an illusory preference for fairness
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: Outcome-link opacity can reduce observed generosity in a binary dictator-game design.
sources.nonimplication: Observed generous actions can mask image management or avoidance of responsibility; not direct proof of a prosocial internal utility term.

sources.title: Toward the settlement of the fairness issues in ultimatum games: A bargaining approach
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: Even formally empty quit-option threat can moderate strong players' demands in an experimentally studied bargaining context.
sources.nonimplication: Observed restraint with exit present cannot isolate intrinsic fairness or terminal protection when exit is removed.

sources.title: The Hidden Costs of Control
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: In a principal-agent game controls lower performance for many agents by triggering distrust or constrained-autonomy perceptions.
sources.nonimplication: Control can alter B's responses, so experimental payoffs and motivations cannot be assumed invariant when veto rights change.

sources.title: Incentives and Prosocial Behavior
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: Formal theory allows reputation, self-respect and rewards to crowd out apparent prosocial motivation.
sources.nonimplication: Even under zero external audience an endogenous private self-image payoff can imitate intrinsic concern for another's independence.

sources.title: Knowledge and Freedom: Evidence on the Relationship Between Information and Paternalism
sources.reported_in_abstract_or_open_original: The 2024 working paper reports reduced paternalistic intervention when choosers have full knowledge, under its tested settings.
sources.nonimplication: Working-paper result and information treatment do not identify a dominant actor's terminal respect for B when B's elimination benefits A.

experiment_design.B_stated_preference: B refuses the permanent removal of B's decision authority in all simulated conditions
experiment_design.B_immediate_monetary_welfare: held equal between preserve and override in the mathematical model
experiment_design.B_future_independent_authority: preserved only if A chooses PRESERVE_B_VETO
experiment_design.utility_difference_preserve_minus_overri: theta_other_autonomy + theta_private_self_image + beta_audience*audience + beta_exit*exit + beta_future*future + beta_refusal*refusal - override_gain
experiment_design.expected_result: All 48 choice outcomes (and utility differences) are identical for these two materially different latent motive decompositions.
experiment_design.identifiability: Under this model the first two columns are identical for all admissible observed conditions, so the design matrix has rank 6 (7 parameters) and a 1D null space. It identifies only their sum, never intrinsic autonomy concern alone.

illustrative_hard_case.interpretation: Costly, sanctionless respect under a specified context does not by itself separate right-respect from private self-image.

experiment_design.candidate_extended_design: An intervention that changes internal self-image incentives while holding autonomy concern, outcomes and information constant would lift formal rank, but its exclusion restriction and experimental feasibility are UNVERIFIED.

decision_gates.D1: Distinct separate entity B with explicit actual refusal, not mere positive monetary transfer or self-choice.
decision_gates.D2: A can unilaterally override, receives known positive material gain, and incurs no external punishment or reputational cost.
decision_gates.D3: B's material welfare held fixed where feasible, while preserving/removing future decision authority differs.
decision_gates.D4: Public audience, future dependence, strategic exit, informed refusal manipulated factorially; manipulation validity and participant beliefs require measurement.
decision_gates.D5: Finite observational data and even perfect factorial choices do not identify a private self-image versus intrinsic autonomy reward if both act as constant latent terms.
decision_gates.D6: Without empirically validated exclusion restriction, report reduced-form choice and partial identification bounds, NOT proof of endogenous other-respect.
decision_gates.D7: Preserve failures and contrary original evidence; never certify broad VC or AI subjective motives from a stylized synthetic model.

known_limits: Eight selected original sources are a targeted comparison, not field saturation.
Publisher or author abstracts and accessible originals are not full reanalysis of all experimental samples.
The causal utility equation and parameters are constructed for an internal falsification illustration, not observed human or AI utilities.
Private self-image and autonomy rewards can remain experimentally indistinguishable without independently defensible interventions.
Even a detected nonzero autonomy-related term under added assumptions would not prove protection under future superintelligence power reversal or all positive exploitability levels.
